title: Head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI): Until the inspection protocol for the attacked sites is formulated, the Agency cannot claim to conduct inspections.
text:
Head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI): Until the inspection protocol for the attacked sites is formulated, the Agency cannot claim to conduct inspections."

"🔆🔅Mohammad Eslami on Wednesday, August 26, at a ceremony unveiling knowledge-based achievements on the occasion of Government Week, in Tehran, responded to a question from IRNA regarding the latest interactions with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and whether Iran has any undeclared activity at sites such as the Kooh-Kalang site, which the U.S. President had previously threatened to bomb."

""

"Mohammad Eslami, Head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization: "These threats serve as a lesson for history that international organizations are toys in the hands of the hegemonic system and the arrogance of the United States and the Zionists. The IAEA has its own laws and statutes, and the Director General of the Agency has specific duties. We expect and hope that they will no longer abuse international organizations, exert pressure on them, threaten their officials, and that they will be allowed to act according to their own regulations.""

"Mohammad Eslami, Head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization: "Our performance has been based on the safeguards and regulations of the Agency. The facilities that have now been subjected to military strikes were all registered with the IAEA, and the Agency has been conducting continuous inspections of them. The fact that the Agency does not protest or condemn these attacks calls its competence and independence into question.""

"Mohammad Eslami, Head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization: "In the current situation, the Agency has conducted the necessary inspections according to safeguards at facilities that have not been attacked. However, regarding the facilities that have been attacked, the law passed by the Iranian Parliament serves as our criterion. The Agency must clarify its duty regarding the security status of the sites and announce what protocol it has for sites that come under military attack. In a situation where the Agency has no such protocol and also takes no stance, it is only the U.S. and Israel that are exerting pressure for the Agency to visit and inspect the destroyed sites. The reason for this pressure is that they want to see what has happened to these sites as a result of the military operation they conducted.""

"Mohammad Eslami, Head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization: "Our country's situation is still a war situation, and it is not yet such that one could assume the war has ended and the security of the sites has been established. The law passed by the Iranian Parliament is our criterion, and we have informed the Agency of this matter according to that same law. The Agency is well aware that under these circumstances, as long as the regulations and protocol for inspecting sites that have been subjected to military attack have not been formulated, approved, and communicated, it cannot claim to conduct inspections.
